items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
COR-TRY-25-032, Quarterly Summary of Tenders/Quotations and Requests for Proposals Approved by the Chief Administrative Officer
notes:
Nicole Neil, Acting Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer provided a brief overview of the report. 

Responding to an inquiry about the Region’s procurement practices and how, in light of ongoing trade tensions, the Region’s approach supports buying local, Mathieu Goetzke, Acting Chief Administrative Officer explained that international trade agreements do not permit local preference, with only narrow exceptions. While the Region cannot impose restrictions on Canadian content, there are still opportunities to support the local economy by encouraging local suppliers and service providers to participate in competitive processes.

Further clarification was sought on whether a municipality could limit procurement to contractors within its boundaries. N. Neil responded that local trade agreements prohibit such restrictions and emphasized the importance of balancing local support with fairness to neighbouring municipalities.

Responding to a question on the report’s highlights. N. Neil explained that the Region prioritizes best overall value, which considers both price and service quality, depending on the procurement method used. M. Goetzke further outlined the differences between a Request for Proposal (RFP) and a Request for Tender (RFT) process.

The Committee discussed the topic of lowest cost and deliberated on whether to revisit the Region’s current approach. The Committee requested that Finance staff report back with additional information on this matter. N. Neil acknowledged the direction.

The report was received for information.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
COR-CFN-25-018, Q3 2025 Plan and Financial Update
notes:
Connie MacDonald, Commissioner, Resident Experience, Strategy and Communications introduced the report and invited N. Neil to provide the financial update. N. Neil reviewed the key highlights of the financial results and spoke to the declining trend in Regional Development Charge (RDC) collections.  

The Committee deliberated on the report.

Responding to a question from the Committee about the status of the reserve fund. N. Neil confirmed that while the current position aligns with earlier projections, it remains below the desired level. She noted that the Tax Stabilization Reserve had an opening balance of $11.4 million, with $2.5 million committed through the 2025 budget process, leaving a balance of 5M after absorbing this deficit forecast. She added that staff are examining options to replenish the reserve, including the use of year-end surpluses, and are reviewing the policy to ensure appropriate contingency levels are maintained.

A member of the Committee asked about the 62% revenue shortfall and whether it relates to Bills 17 and 23, and if the Province is aware or could be engaged to help address the shortfall. N. Neil responded that similar decreases are being observed across other municipalities and that the Region continues to engage in discussions with its municipal partners on this matter.

The Committee further discussed intergovernmental collaboration and the impact of inaccurate student population estimates on financial forecasting.

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-25-018, Q3 2025 Plan and Financial Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the Q3 Plan and Financial Update as set out in report COR-CFN-25-018 dated November 4, 2025: Receive the Q3 Update for information that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Strategic Plan 2023-2027; and Amend the 2025 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix D.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the Q3 Plan and Financial Update as set out in report COR-CFN-25-018 dated November 4, 2025:

  1. Receive the Q3 Update for information that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Strategic Plan 2023-2027; and
  2. Amend the 2025 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix D.
